title: Kafka trip-replay event (Week 5 producer -> Structured Streaming)
description: Execution plan W4 D5 (Mounika, proposed -- Krishna and Lahari to confirm at the Week 5 sync). Two kinds of event on one topic, mirroring the fact/query event-stream design D-020 already built for the batch feature pipeline (src/pipeline/features.py) rather than inventing a second shape for the same idea: a 'query' event is a leg being created (what the champion model predicts on), a 'fact' event is a leg finishing (what feeds the broadcast history the next query needs). Replaying both kinds of the same historical events Stage 2 (Mounika) already reconstructed keeps the streaming layer and the batch layer answering to the same D-020 contract instead of two independently-invented ones.

event_id.description: One per emitted Kafka message. Consumer-side idempotency key -- a replayed or redelivered message must not double-count into the broadcast history or double-fire an alert (the same idempotency reasoning D-017 already gives the mock TMS's external_ref).

kind.description: query: a leg is created, at trip_creation_time -- carries what the model predicts on. fact: a leg finishes, at od_end_time -- carries the outcome that becomes usable history for every query after it. Same two kinds, same ordering rule (facts sort before queries at equal event_time) as D-020's as_of_history.

event_time.description: The REAL historical timestamp being replayed (trip_creation_time for a query, od_end_time for a fact) -- not the wall-clock time the producer actually sent the message, which time-compresses the ~26-day observation window. Kafka's own message timestamp is the wall-clock send time; this field is what streaming's as-of join keys off, exactly as Stage 4 keys off it in batch.

leg_id.description: D-020's key: trip_uuid|od_start_time|corridor_id. A trip can repeat a corridor on a different day, so the key needs the departure time to stay unique -- reused here rather than redefined, the same reasoning D-026 (Lahari, Week 4) gives for reusing time_split rather than reimplementing it.

gap_min.description: fact only -- actual_time - planned_min, D-020's TARGETS.

is_delayed.description: fact only -- D-003's label, gap_min > (DELAY_THRESHOLD - 1) * planned_min.
